issues.description: Method 'acceptSupplyDelivery' has inconsistent parameter lists across artifacts. The problem statement and UML declare acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (four parameters). However, the provided example call in the template (Main.java) and the reference implementation in SealSaloon.java use a three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity). This discrepancy will confuse students about which signature to implement and can cause compilation or test failures if the implemented signature does not match the grader's expectation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across all materials. Preferred fix: update the problem statement and UML to specify the three-parameter signature used by the template and solution: acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (omit the supplierName parameter from the spec). Alternatively, update the template and reference solution to implement the four-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and adjust example calls accordingly. Ensure the corrected signature is used in the problem text, UML, template examples, and reference solution so students have one clear specification.
